responses: At a counter, Ponticius offered two hundred gold for the Sun Ruins job, half now and half upon return of the artifact. Max countered with three hundred and said they would leave tonight, while Arin urged him to accept because they needed the coin. Ponticius scowled, laughed, and settled on two fifty; Max agreed and took the pouch.

messages.speaker: Ponticius
messages.text: "Two hundred gold for the Sun Ruins. Half now, half when you bring back the artifact." He slides a pouch across the counter.

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: "Make it three hundred and we leave tonight."

messages.speaker: Ponticius
messages.text: He scowls, then laughs. "Two fifty. Final offer."

messages.speaker: Arin
messages.text: "Take it, Max. We need the coin."

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: "Deal." I take the pouch.

responses: At the abandoned mill, rain hammered the roof and the wheel groaned in the flood as Lady Ashworth accused Max of being followed despite her instruction to come alone. Max denied it and asked what she had for him, and Lady Ashworth handed him a sealed letter proving the governor ordered the fire, warning him to guard it with his life.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Rain hammers the roof of the abandoned mill. Somewhere below, the wheel groans in the flood.

messages.speaker: Lady Ashworth
messages.text: "You were followed. I told you to come alone."

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: "Nobody followed me. What do you have for me?"

messages.speaker: Lady Ashworth
messages.text: She hands over a sealed letter. "Proof that the governor ordered the fire. Guard it with your life."

responses: Max knelt by the fallen guard and searched his pockets, finding iron keys and a folded duty roster. Vex warned that the next patrol was in ten minutes and told him to move, so Max unlocked the cell door and pulled the prisoner out. The thin old man clutched Max’s arm and whispered a name: Corvin.

responses: Arin said he did not trust Oskar because he had lied about the map, and Max answered that they would watch him and still needed his boat. Oskar pushed off from the bank without a word, and the reeds closed behind the boat. The mood was tense and wary.
